Part of #295

## Question

Evaluate the authentication and transport stack for SurveyBeat's remote Streamable HTTP MCP server (`/mcp`) on `MainWorker`:
- Compare Better Auth's `@better-auth/mcp` plugin (OAuth 2.1 + PKCE + consent screen over SurveyBeat's existing Better Auth 1.7.25 on D1, ADR 0022/0024) against `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider`.
- Evaluate MCP server libraries compatible with Cloudflare Workers and Effect 4.1.x (stateless per-request handler, Effect Schema tool input/output validation, `nodejs_compat`).
- Confirm how an authenticated OAuth token resolves to a SurveyBeat `Person`, active Organization, and `Actor` roles—including immediate revocation when a Person is removed or banned (ADR 0023, ADR 0024).

## Output

A written research note recommending the OAuth + MCP transport stack and D1/DO storage changes.

## Notes from review (2026-11-20)

- ADR 0023 removed ADR 0010's `revoked_session` deny list: revocation is deleting the session row. The MCP token path needs its own equivalent, so a revoked or deleted grant fails the next request.
- **Check that the Person is active and not banned** on every MCP request. ADR 0024 says Better Auth enforces `banned` only on its own endpoints, and a long-lived OAuth token deserves the stricter check.
- Confirm the real package name of Better Auth's MCP / OAuth provider support (as far as we know, the `mcp` plugin in `better-auth/plugins` or `@better-auth/oauth-provider`) at the 1.7.25 pin.

# Effect HTTP API on Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, and Workflows

Research for issue #9 (map #1). Researched on 2026-11-07. Throwaway branch, never merged.

Question: how mature is running Effect, and the HttpApi module (declare the API once, derive the server and a typed client), on Workers, Durable Objects (DOs) and Workflows? SPEC §6.1 fixes Effect, Effect Schema and the HttpApi module. §6.3 requires the domain package to run in plain Node tests.

## Verdict

- **Target `effect@4.1.2`** (npm `latest`, published 2026-11-02). Pin every `@effect/*` package to the same version. Effect 4 shipped as 4.0.0 on 2026-10-01 and is an LTS line. Do not start on 3.x.
- **Workers run the HttpApi module.** `HttpRouter.toWebHandler` is the first-party adapter, and its own API docs carry Cloudflare-specific instructions. A real HttpApi Worker bundles to about 86 KiB gzip and starts in about 55–60 ms of local CPU, against a 1 s limit (my measurements below).
- **First-party coverage stops at HTTP and SQL.** Effect ships `@effect/sql-d1` and `@effect/sql-sqlite-do`. It ships nothing for DO classes, Workflow entrypoints, Queues or bindings. You either write a thin bridge yourself, or use Alchemy v2 (`alchemy@2.0.0-beta.85`), which is Effect-native and already covers Workers, DOs, Workflows, D1, KV and Queues. SPEC already fixes Alchemy as the infrastructure tool.
- **Maturity risk is real but bounded.** Every module involved (`effect/http`, `effect/http-api`, `effect/sql`, `effect/workflow`, `effect/schema/Model`, and all `@effect/sql-*` drivers) is tagged `@stability unstable`. That tag allows breaking changes in minor releases. Several Workers-specific bugs were fixed in Sept–Oct 2026, and one fix for request scopes is still open. Pin exact versions and read changelogs before you bump.

## 1. Effect version and what changed in v4

| Fact | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `effect` dist-tags: `latest: 4.1.2`, `prev: 3.22.4`. 4.0.0 published 2026-10-01, 4.1.0 on 2026-10-29, 4.1.2 on 2026-11-02 | `npm view effect dist-tags time` |
| "Effect 4.x is a long-term support (LTS) release, with at least three years of bug and security fixes." Bug fixes until Sept 2029 or one year after 5.0, whichever is later | `effect@4.1.2` README; https://effect.website/blog/releases/effect/40 |
| v4 development moved from `Effect-TS/effect-smol` (now archived, "Effect V4 Has Moved") into `Effect-TS/effect` `main`. v3 lives on the `v3` branch | https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect-smol README |
| Minimal program: 3.x 35.6 kB vs 4.x 7.1 kB (min+gzip). Throughput 6.4× higher, 86 % less memory per fiber | https://effect.website/blog/releases/effect/40 |
| Requires TypeScript ≥ 5.9 and `strict`. Node ≥ 22.19 when running on Node | `effect@4.1.2` README |

What changed for the platform packages (https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/main/MIGRATION.md):

- **`@effect/platform`, `@effect/rpc`, `@effect/cluster`, `@effect/sql` and others were merged into `effect`.** HTTP is now `effect/http` and HttpApi is now `effect/http-api`. SQL is `effect/sql`, workflows are `effect/workflow`, and so on. `@effect/platform` stays on its v3 line (`0.97.x`). Do not install it with v4.
- **Lockstep versioning.** Every remaining package (`@effect/platform-*`, `@effect/sql-*`, `@effect/ai-*`, `@effect/vitest`, `@effect/opentelemetry`) shares one version with `effect`.
- **Unstable module paths lost their `unstable` segment.** Use `effect/http`, not `effect/unstable/http`, and no compatibility exports remain. The modules are still `@stability unstable`, which means "new features in patch releases and breaking changes in minor releases". The migration guide also says "Moving these modules does not stabilize their APIs." The unstable list includes `http`, `http-api`, `rpc`, `schema` (sub-modules such as `Model`), `sql` and `workflow`. Every module in packages other than `effect` is unstable too.
- Core renames that affect every file: `Context.Tag` → `Context.Service`, `Schema.TaggedError` keeps its name, `catch*` combinators were renamed, and `Runtime<R>` was removed. The links are in MIGRATION.md.
- There is no `@effect/platform-cloudflare` and no `@effect/cloudflare` package (both 404 on npm). Workers use the platform-neutral `effect/http` directly.

# Better Auth owns sign-in sessions in D1

Sign-in is WorkOS AuthKit today: the Worker seals a WorkOS session into `__Host-surveybeat-session`, verifies the access token locally, and D1 indexes WorkOS users and organizations (`docs/infra.md`, ADR 0010). Issue #200 replaces the provider with Better Auth, the library rat-stack runs on the same Alchemy pin, so SurveyBeat owns its user and session rows in D1 and stops calling a provider on every sign-in.

**What moves.** A new package, `packages/auth`, owns the Better Auth options: `basePath: "/auth"`, the email one-time-code plugin, a 30-day session, and the `__Host-surveybeat-session` cookie with `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/` and no `Domain`. The Worker keeps its own HTTP surface (`/auth/login`, `/auth/logout`, `/auth/session`, `/auth/organization`, `/auth/organization/choose`) and reaches Better Auth through the `IdentityProvider` port, so the Foldkit app never talks to Better Auth's default client routes. `better-auth` is pinned at `1.7.11` and `@alchemy.run/better-auth` at `2.0.0-beta.85` next to the existing Alchemy pin.

**What does not move.** The Organization is still the Durable Object tenant (ADR 0006); Better Auth's organization plugin is not adopted and there is no one-to-one WorkOS organization map any more. The Better Auth user id replaces `AuthUserId`, and `PersonId` stays SurveyBeat's own id: one human can be a different Person in each Organization, so `session.user.id` is never treated as a `PersonId`. Organization admin stays a fact in the Organization object (ADR 0003). An email links a Person or passes the create-organization allowlist only when the provider verified it and it is printable ASCII (ADR 0002); the allowlist file stays `infra/org-creation-allowlist.yaml`.

**Revocation.** ADR 0010's requirement stands: a revoked session fails the next request. Sign-out deletes the Better Auth session row in D1. The `revoked_session` deny list stays until a test shows a deleted session is refused on the next request with no extra row; then the row and that part of ADR 0010 go in the same change.

**Store and secret.** Better Auth writes its own `auth_user`, `auth_session`, `auth_account` and `auth_verification` tables in the same D1 database as the people index, kept apart by that prefix so nothing sits beside `person_index` or `organization_index` by accident. The tables come from SurveyBeat's own numbered migration (`packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations/0008_better_auth.sql`), not from a deploy-time schema push, so the schema is reviewed and reversible like every other D1 change; the Alchemy `BetterAuth` resource therefore runs with `migrate: false` and the D1 adapter reads the raw binding, so no connection string or second database exists. The resource provisions its own signing secret as an Alchemy random resource that is bound into the Worker environment, the way `WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD` is today, so no secret is checked in or set by hand.

**Deferred.** Enterprise SSO (SAML or OIDC) and Directory Sync (SCIM) leave this change; SPEC §5.6 and §6.1 name them deferred until a later issue. Google and Microsoft stay on the sign-in screen only if Better Auth can configure them inside the Worker; a provider that cannot is called out rather than silently dropped.

## Considered options

- **Keep WorkOS and add Better Auth beside it.** Rejected: two providers mean two session truths and two revocation paths.
- **Adopt Better Auth's organization plugin as the tenant.** Rejected: it would put a second source of truth next to the Organization Durable Object, contradicting ADR 0006.
- **Treat `session.user.id` as the Person id, as rat-stack does.** Rejected: a Person is per Organization here, and the same human is several Persons.

## Consequences

- SurveyBeat stores users and sessions in D1 instead of indexing WorkOS; `@workos-inc/node`, `WORKOS_API_KEY`, `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` and the cookie password that sealed WorkOS sessions go away at cutover.
- The Worker must answer better-auth's endpoint surface internally, and CI needs an in-memory Better Auth layer for tests, which `memoryAuth` provides.
- Migration is staged: the pins, options and in-memory sign-in test land first with WorkOS still serving, then the D1 session store, then the port and routes, then revocation and the docs.
# The sign-in port answers who is signed in, not where

ADR 0022 moved sign-in into Better Auth and left the WorkOS-shaped `IdentityProvider` in place. That port does two jobs at once: it reads a session, and it asks the provider where the person belongs — an AuthKit organization, an organization-selection prompt, a membership with a role. Better Auth has no organizations at all, and SurveyBeat never wanted the provider to own them (ADR 0006, ADR 0003). This ADR splits the two jobs so the route swap in the next slice has a port to talk to.

**The session port.** `SessionIdentityProvider` in `packages/domain/src/people/SessionIdentity.ts` has two calls: `authenticate(cookie)` returns the `Identity` plus the provider session id, or `Unauthenticated`; `revokeSession(sessionId)` deletes the session. `BetterAuthIdentityProvider` implements it by reading `auth.api.getSession` with the `__Host-surveybeat-session` cookie and, on revoke, deleting the `auth_session` row by id. Nothing is sealed any more: the cookie value is Better Auth's own session token, so a session check costs one D1 read rather than a provider call, and there is no refresh that re-issues a cookie. The WorkOS-shaped `IdentityProvider` keeps serving `/auth/*` until the routes move; then it, `CodeExchange`, `ProviderSession.sealed`, `refresh`, `logoutUrl`, `authorizationUrl` and `authenticateWithCode` are deleted.

**The picker.** A picker only exists because a human can be several Persons. That fact already lives in `people_index` and the Organization's own people table, and `decideSignIn` already builds the candidate list from `PeopleIndex` and `OrganizationPeople`. So the picker stops being a provider concept: no AuthKit organization id, no `OrganizationSelectionRequired`, no pending-authentication token, and no provider round trip when someone chooses. `/auth/organization/choose` resolves the chosen `OrganizationId` against the same candidates and sets nothing in the cookie, because the session is one session across organizations. The `workos_organization_id` column, `organizationByWorkos` and `workosOrganizationOf` go with it.

**Membership.** The provider kept a second copy of membership: `createOrganization`, `ensureMembership`, `setMembershipRole`, `deactivateMembership`. All four leave the port. The Organization is the Durable Object tenant, its `person` rows are the membership, and `organizationAdmin` is a fact in that object (ADR 0003). Nothing writes an admin flag to an auth user, and nothing syncs a role outward, because there is nowhere outward to sync to. The one provider-side id that used to be stored in `people_index` (`auth_user_id`) becomes the Better Auth user id; `PersonId` stays SurveyBeat's own id and `session.user.id` is never treated as one.

**The HTTP surface.** `/auth/logout`, `/auth/session`, `/auth/organization` and `/auth/organization/choose` keep their paths and their responses. `/auth/login` still starts sign-in, but it can no longer redirect to a hosted AuthKit page: the Foldkit app asks for an email address, posts it to Better Auth's code endpoint, and the code returns the session cookie that `/auth/session` already reads. `/auth/callback` exists only because AuthKit redirects, so it goes; the paths in #200 never listed it. Sign-out deletes the session row and answers 303 to the app, since there is no hosted logout page left to redirect to.

**The chosen Organization.** A session is one session across Organizations, so the choice cannot live in the cookie and cannot be an auth-provider concept either. It lives in `auth_session_organization` (`session_id` primary key references `auth_session` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`), one row per session, written only by `/auth/organization/choose` after the choice has been checked against the same candidates. `SessionIdentityProvider` carries `chosenOrganization` and `chooseOrganization`; revoking the session deletes the row with it, and nothing else is ever written. `/auth/session` falls back to the single linked Person when no choice has been made yet, so the first sign-in needs no extra round trip.

**The email code.** The sign-in form needs somewhere to send the address and the code without the browser calling Better Auth directly. `/auth/email-code` and `/auth/email-code/verify` are our own API endpoints; the second hands Better Auth's session token back through `SessionIdentityProvider.verifySignInCode`, and the Worker sets `__Host-surveybeat-session` from it. Everything else under `/auth/*` is Better Auth's own handler, mounted in `MainWorker`.

**Revocation.** Deleting the row is the revocation. `revoked_session`, `isSessionRevoked` and the deny-list half of ADR 0010 are gone: `D1Auth.test.ts` proves a deleted session is refused on the next request while `auth_session_organization` and `person_index` gain no row.

## Considered options

- **Keep the WorkOS-shaped port and implement it over Better Auth.** Rejected: it would need an authorization URL, an organization-selection exchange and membership writes that Better Auth cannot perform, so the adapter would either lie or die on paths the routes still call.
- **Keep the organization picker in the provider by adopting Better Auth's organization plugin.** Rejected in ADR 0022: a second tenant next to the Durable Object.
- **Sync Better Auth's user id into `person_index` as the membership key and drop the Person's email lookup.** Rejected: an email still links an unlinked Person before the first sign-in, and `person_index` already holds that evidence.
- **Rename `AuthUserId` in the same change as the port.** Rejected for now: the rename touches every domain, D1 and Durable Object call site, and the live WorkOS routes would have to be rewritten twice. The port and the adapter land first; the rename lands with the route swap.

## Consequences

- `BetterAuthIdentityProvider` and its tests land while WorkOS still serves, so the port is proven against both the in-memory adapter and the real D1 migration before a single route changes.
- The route swap is smaller: `AuthHandlers` loses the callback handler and the state cookie, and `MainWorker` provides `SessionIdentityProvider` instead of `IdentityProvider`.
- `d1-migrations/0003_people_index.sql` and `0008_better_auth.sql` are rewritten in place: `workos_user_id` is `auth_user_id`, `workos_organization_id` and `revoked_session` are gone, and `auth_session_organization` is new. Any stage that already ran the old files needs its dev schema reset once; the migration history is checked at deploy and refuses a silent rewrite.
- The sign-in screen gains an email field, which the web app does not have today; that is the first UI change this issue makes.
# Better Auth's magic-link, admin, organization and passkey plugins are enabled

ADR 0022 adopted Better Auth for sign-in with the email one-time-code plugin only, and rejected the organization plugin as the tenant. This ADR adds three more plugins and the passkey plugin to the same instance. The tenant decision does not change: the Organization Durable Object is still the system of record for Teams, People and survey content (ADR 0006), and the plugins are an auth-plane capability rather than a second tenant.

**What is enabled.** `packages/auth/src/options.ts` builds one plugin list for every instance, `authOptions`, so the Worker's `BetterAuth` resource and `createAuth`/`memoryAuth` in tests cannot drift:

- `magicLink` with `MAGIC_LINK_TTL_SECONDS` (300 seconds). The link is delivered through the same `EmailSender` the invitation and sign-in code use, so a non-production stage records it in `captured_email` and production sends it. Better Auth consumes a token on the first verification, so one link mints at most one session.
- `admin` with `defaultRole: "user"` and `adminRoles: ["admin"]`. This role is the auth plane's own and is not the Organization admin: Organization admins stay a fact in the Organization object (ADR 0003). No product route reads `user.role`.
- `organization` with `allowUserToCreateOrganization: false`. Creating an Organization stays the allowlisted flow in `packages/domain` and the Organization Durable Object; the plugin's `auth_organization`, `auth_member` and `auth_invitation` rows are not the tenant and no product route treats them as one.
- `passkey` (`@better-auth/passkey`, pinned with `better-auth`). The relying party is derived from the instance's base URL, so a stage's passkey registrations and the local stage on `localhost` are scoped to their own origin.

**Store.** The plugin columns and tables are a numbered D1 migration, `packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations/0009_better_auth_plugins.sql`, in the same style as ADR 0022: `auth_user` gains `role`, `banned`, `banReason` and `banExpires`; `auth_session` gains `impersonatedBy` and `activeOrganizationId`; four new tables (`auth_organization`, `auth_member`, `auth_invitation`, `auth_passkey`) keep the `auth_` prefix. Columns and indexes are the schema Better Auth 1.7.11 generates for these plugins with SurveyBeat's model names, so no deploy-time push exists and `migrate: false` still holds.

**Surface.** The Worker forwards every `/auth/*` path it does not answer itself to Better Auth, so the plugin endpoints (`/auth/sign-in/magic-link`, `/auth/magic-link/verify`, `/auth/passkey/*`, `/auth/admin/*`, `/auth/organization/*`) are reachable on the Worker's own origin without a client library. The exact paths SurveyBeat answers, `/auth/organization` and `/auth/organization/choose` among them, keep priority; the plugin's nested routes do not collide with them.

## Considered options

- **Keep email codes as the only sign-in.** Rejected: the plugins are requested, and a mailed link is the shape that survives a mail client that breaks a code across lines.
- **Adopt the organization plugin as the tenant.** Still rejected, for the reason in ADR 0022: two sources of truth for Teams and People.
- **Let any signed-in user create a Better Auth organization.** Rejected: Organization creation is allowlisted (`infra/org-creation-allowlist.yaml`), and a second creation path would bypass that list.

## Consequences

- ADR 0022's "the organization plugin is not adopted" sentence is superseded by this ADR; its other decisions stand.
- The mail sender has a second delivery, `sendMagicLink`, beside `sendSignInCode`.
- The admin plugin's `banned` flag is enforced by Better Auth on its own endpoints. SurveyBeat's per-request check is unchanged: the Person must be active in the chosen Organization.
# Being an Organization admin grants no access to any Team's Results

The Organization admin role (WorkOS's org-level `admin`) covers administration only: Teams, Leads, and People. Seeing a Team's Results, comments, or Actions requires a Membership in that Team, whatever the person's Organization role. Admins are often the people members worry about most. If the admin role could read every Team's Results, it would undercut "trust before features" and put leadership roll-ups (Release 3) in through a side door.

### 5.6 Administration

- **Sign-in.** Sign-in is Better Auth with an email code (ADR 0022, ADR 0023). Google, Microsoft and enterprise SSO are later additions, not part of the first release.
- **Directory sync.** Directory sync (SCIM) creates and removes people and can map directory groups to teams, and is not in the first release. When a person is removed, they lose access immediately. Their memberships end on that date, and history stays intact.
- **Roles and permissions.** Organization-level roles are a fact in the Organization's own data: an admin flag (admin, member). Team-level roles (lead, member, viewer) live there too, because they belong to the domain. Permission checks are one function of (person, action, resource), defined in one place and tested as a table.
- **Audit log.** The system records admin and lead actions, such as changing privacy settings, changing anonymity modes, exporting data, and adding leads, in a store inside SurveyBeat.
- **Billing.** Not in the first release. Design the model so that seats or teams per organization can be counted later.

### 5.7 Integrations and API

- **Slack app and Microsoft Teams app.** Members can answer from the messages. Leads get the results summary in a channel they choose. A slash command or message action shows the team's current health.
- **Public API.** A small, versioned HTTP API, authenticated with organization API keys, that returns results and actions. All privacy rules apply.
- **MCP server.** A remote MCP server lets a lead use an AI assistant to ask about their teams' results and manage actions. It enforces the same permissions and privacy thresholds as the web app, because it calls the same domain services.
- **Webhooks.** Webhooks for "round results ready" and "action created or updated".

### 5.8 Product surfaces outside the app

- A marketing landing page, a pricing page that can be a placeholder, and legal pages for privacy, terms, and the data processing agreement. The old app had legal page stubs. The rebuild needs real text before any external customer uses it.
- Transactional emails for invitations, reminders, results-ready notices, and action updates. They must look good in the major email clients and in dark mode.

## 6. Platform and architecture

Everything runs on Cloudflare. No Next.js, no Vercel, and no separate cloud provider for compute or data. Sign-in runs on Better Auth inside the Main Worker, so the Slack and Microsoft Teams platforms are the only required external services.

### 6.1 Fixed technology choices

| Concern | Choice | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Infrastructure as code | alchemy.run | Every Cloudflare resource, binding, secret, and custom domain is declared in TypeScript with Alchemy. No dashboard changes. No Terraform. No hand-edited wrangler config. |
| Runtime | Cloudflare Workers | One Worker serves the API and the static web app (Workers static assets). Add more Workers only when a job needs a different runtime profile, such as a queue consumer. |
| Business logic | Effect | All domain logic, data access, and integrations are Effect programs. Errors, dependencies, retries, and timeouts are typed. Domain services are Effect services with layers that can be swapped in tests. |
| Schemas | Effect Schema | One schema definition per domain type is shared by the API, the client, the database layer, and the AI tool definitions. External data is parsed at the boundary, and internal code trusts the types. |
| HTTP API | Effect's platform HTTP API module | The API is declared once. The server implementation and a typed client for the web app both come from that declaration. |
| Web app | React single-page app built with Vite | Client-side routing with a typed router, such as TanStack Router. Answer pages and email landing pages must render fast without a heavy bundle. Split them into their own small entry point. |
| UI components | Base UI | Unstyled, accessible primitives. Build a small design system of your own on top (tokens, typography, and a dozen composed components). Tailwind CSS for styling is fine. Charts need an accessible library or hand-built SVG, and each chart needs a table view. |
| Authentication | Better Auth on D1, email codes | The Worker serves `/auth/*`: an email-code start and verify, a session cookie, and sign-out. The session is checked on every request against D1 and the Organization's Durable Object. ADR 0022 and ADR 0023. |
| Email | Cloudflare Email Service | Sends invitations, reminders, and notices. Inbound email routing is optional, for reply-to-answer later. If Cloudflare email sending cannot meet deliverability needs, decide on a fallback and record it. |
| AI | Cloudflare Workers AI, through AI Gateway | Comment redaction, theme grouping, discussion guides, and "ask your results". AI Gateway handles caching, rate limits, logging policy, and model swaps. Never send raw comments to a model that keeps them. |

### 6.2 Cloudflare building blocks and their jobs

The recommended layout follows. Departures are fine when they make the system simpler, but write down the reason.

- **Durable Object per organization, with SQLite storage, as the system of record.** Each organization's people, teams, pulses, rounds, submissions, results, and actions live in that organization's own Durable Object. This gives hard tenant isolation, strongly consistent writes, and plain SQL for analytics within one organization. Survey data is small, so a single object's storage limit is far away. An organization with 5,000 people answering weekly for 5 years stays well under it. Check this number against current Cloudflare limits before you commit.
- **Durable Object per open round** (optional, decide during the build). It counts participation, rejects double submissions, and owns the round's state machine. If the organization object handles this load well, skip the extra object.
- **D1 for the global index.** This holds what must be looked up before you know the organization: auth user to Persons, invitation token to organization and round, Slack and Teams workspace to organization, and API keys. Keep it small. No survey content goes here.
- **Cloudflare Workflows for the round lifecycle.** Each round is a durable workflow. It waits until the open time, sends invitations in batches, waits, sends reminders, closes, computes results, and notifies. Workflows give retries and resumption after crashes, and each step must be idempotent.
- **Cron Triggers** run once an hour to create the next round for each active pulse. This job is idempotent. Running it twice creates no duplicate rounds.
- **Queues** buffer outbound messages (email, Slack, Teams) and inbound webhooks, with retries and a dead-letter queue.
- **R2** stores exports and generated PDFs, and backups of each organization's data on a schedule.
- **KV** holds rarely changing configuration and caches, if needed. Do not use it for sessions that must be revoked at once.
- **Workers Analytics Engine** stores product metrics (send counts, open rates, answer latency). It must never contain answers.
- **Turnstile** protects the public link answer page against bots.
- **Secrets Store, or Worker secrets managed through Alchemy**, holds the Slack and Teams credentials.

### 6.3 Code organization

- One repository and one package manager workspace. Suggested packages are the domain (pure Effect services and schemas, with no Cloudflare imports), the Cloudflare adapters (Durable Objects, D1, Queues, Workflows, and email, each implementing a domain interface), the API, the web app, the infrastructure definition, and the email templates.
- The domain package must run in plain Node tests without Cloudflare. Adapter packages are tested against local Cloudflare emulation (Miniflare, through Alchemy's dev mode or the Vitest integration for Workers).
- Organize modules by domain concept (rounds, privacy, results, actions), not by layer or execution step.

### 6.4 Environments and delivery

- Alchemy stages give every pull request its own preview environment, with its own Workers, D1, and Durable Object namespaces. The preview is removed when the pull request closes.
- `staging` and `production` are Alchemy stages too. Production deploys from the main branch after CI passes.
- CI runs type checking, linting, unit tests, Worker integration tests, the privacy test suite, and an accessibility check on the answer page.
- Errors and traces go to Workers Logs and Workers Observability. Add Sentry only if Cloudflare's tooling is not enough, and then strip all answer content before sending.

# `@modelcontextprotocol/server`

The MCP (Model Context Protocol) TypeScript server SDK. Build MCP servers that expose tools, resources, and prompts.

> **This is v2 of the MCP TypeScript SDK, the stable release line**, implementing the [2026-07-28 MCP spec](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28). It replaces the single `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` package from v1. Found a problem? [Open an issue](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/issues/new?template=v2-feedback.yml).

## Install

```bash
npm install @modelcontextprotocol/server
```

TypeScript ≥6.0 no longer auto-includes `@types/*` — add `"types": ["node"]` to your `tsconfig.json` `compilerOptions` (the published `.d.mts` references `Buffer`).

 * {@linkcode Server}) instance for one serving unit: one HTTP request under
 * {@linkcode createMcpHandler}, or one connection (or one discarded

 * era either entry serves — define your tools, resources and prompts once and
 * serve them to both eras.
 */
type McpServerFactory = (ctx: McpRequestContext) => McpServer | Server | Promise<McpServer | Server>;
/** Caller-provided per-request inputs for {@linkcode McpHttpHandler.fetch} and fetch-shaped legacy handlers ({@linkcode LegacyHttpHandler}). */
interface McpHandlerRequestOptions {
  /**
   * Validated authentication information for the request. Strictly
   * pass-through: the handler never populates this from request headers and
   * performs no token verification of its own.
   */
  authInfo?: AuthInfo;
  /** A pre-parsed JSON request body (e.g. `req.body` from `express.json()`). */
  parsedBody?: unknown;
}

 * `'stateless' | 'reject'` posture only.

MUST

implement OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (

RFC9728

). MCP clients

MUST

use OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata for

authorization server discovery

.

[Navigate to header: Client Registration](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization#client-registration) Client Registration

Before initiating the authorization flow, MCP clients MUST obtain a client ID through one of three registration mechanisms: Client ID Metadata Documents, pre-registration, or Dynamic Client Registration, following the requirements and selection priority defined in [Client Registration](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/client-registration).

MCP clients MUST send this parameter regardless of whether authorization servers support it.

[Navigate to header: Token Requirements](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization#token-requirements) Token Requirements

Access token handling when making requests to MCP servers MUST conform to the requirements defined in [OAuth 2.1 Section 5 “Resource Requests”](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-13#section-5). Specifically:

MCP client

MUST

use the Authorization request header field defined in

OAuth 2.1 Section 5.1.1

:

```
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
```

Note that authorization MUST be included in every HTTP request from client to server.

MUST NOT

be included in the URI query string

```
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: mcp.example.com
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json, text/event-stream
Mcp-Method: tools/list
{
"jsonrpc": "2.0",
"id": 1,
"method": "tools/list",
"params": {
"_meta": {
"io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion": "2026-07-28",
"io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo": {
"name": "ExampleClient",
"version": "1.0.0"
},
"io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities": {}
}
}
}
```

[Navigate to header: Token Handling](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization#token-handling) Token Handling

MCP servers MUST validate that access tokens were issued specifically for them as the intended audience, according to [RFC 8707 Section 2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8707.html#section-2). If validation fails, servers MUST respond according to [OAuth 2.1 Section 5.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-13#section-5.3) error handling requirements. Invalid or expired tokens MUST receive an HTTP 401 response.MCP clients MUST NOT send tokens to the MCP server other than

[Navigate to header: Refresh Tokens](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization#refresh-tokens) Refresh Tokens

This section provides guidance for MCP Clients and MCP Servers when handling or issuing refresh tokens for both OAuth and OpenID Connect.MCP Clients that desire refresh tokens:

MUST

keep refresh tokens confidential in transit and storage as specified in

OAuth 2.1 Section 4.3

SHOULD

include

refresh_token

in their

grant_types

client metadata

MAY

add

offline_access

to the

scope

parameter of the authorization and token requests when the Authorization Server metadata contains it in

scopes_supported

MUST NOT

assume refresh tokens will be issued; the AS retains discretion

MCP Servers (Protected Resources) SHOULD NOT include offline_access in WWW-Authenticate scope or Protected Resource Metadata scopes_supported, as refresh tokens are not a resource requirement.

[Navigate to header: Error Handling](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization#error-handling) Error Handling

Servers MUST return appropriate HTTP status codes for authorization errors:

| Status Code | Description | Usage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | Unauthorized | Authorization required or token invalid |
| 403 | Forbidden | Invalid scopes or insufficient permissions |
| 400 | Bad Request | Malformed authorization request |

[Navigate to header: Scope Challenge Handling](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization#scope-challenge-handling) Scope Challenge Handling

This section covers handling insufficient scope errors during runtime operations when a client already has a token but needs additional permissions. This follows the error handling patterns defined in [OAuth 2.1 Section 5](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-13#section-5) and leverages the metadata fields from [RFC 9728 (OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9728).

[Navigate to header: Advertising CIMD Support](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/client-registration#advertising-cimd-support) Advertising CIMD Support

Authorization servers advertise that they support clients using Client ID Metadata Documents by including the following property in their OAuth Authorization Server metadata:

```
{
"client_id_metadata_document_supported": true
}
```

MCP clients SHOULD check for this capability and MAY fall back to [Dynamic Client Registration](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/client-registration#dynamic-client-registration) or [pre-registration](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/client-registration#pre-registration) if unavailable.

Dynamic Client Registration is deprecated. New implementations should use [Client ID Metadata Documents](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/client-registration#client-id-metadata-documents) instead. This option remains available for backwards compatibility with authorization servers that do not support Client ID Metadata Documents.

MCP clients and authorization servers MAY support the OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration Protocol [RFC7591](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591) to allow MCP clients to obtain OAuth client IDs without user interaction. {"answer":"The MCP plugin lets your app act as an OAuth authorization server and protected resource for [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) clients.

mcp() configures the OAuth provider with MCP resource binding and serves the [RFC 9728](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9728) protected resource metadata.

The well-known URLs are derived from the issuer, so a server with a base path serves them at the issuer-inserted location rather than the bare root.

Better Auth owns OAuth discovery, client registration and discovery, PKCE authorization, resource binding, token issuance and refresh, and protected-resource challenges. The official MCP TypeScript SDK v2 owns the stateless MCP protocol and transport. Configure servers with legacy: "reject", and pin SDK client version negotiation to 2026-07-28 when adopting this profile.

The [RFC 9728](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9728)/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource document is served automatically at the well-known root (and the resource-path-inserted alias). It tells MCP clients which authorization server protects the resource, which scopes it supports, which resource identifier their access tokens must be bound to, and which DPoP proof algorithms are supported.

Set resource to the protected resource identifier MCP clients request and access tokens carry as aud:

With Prisma on PostgreSQL, CockroachDB, or MongoDB, also declare this resource in resources with explicit allowedScopes; see [Resources](https://better-auth.com/docs/plugins/oauth-provider/tokens#resources).

mcp() also registers this identifier as a default client-registration resource. A dynamically registered client is linked to the MCP resource even when its registration request omits the non-standard resources field. Any clientRegistrationDefaultResources you provide are preserved, and the MCP resource is appended once.

[Configuration](https://better-auth.com/docs/plugins/mcp#configuration)

mcp() extends the [OAuth Provider](https://better-auth.com/docs/plugins/oauth-provider/reference#plugin-options) options. All OAuth provider options are passed flat (there is no nested oidcConfig). The required MCP-specific option is resource.

For every client configured through mcp(), the plugin defaults refreshTokenReuseInterval to 30 seconds. This lets a client retry a refresh with the old token and receive the same rotated token response when another request already consumed that refresh token. OAuth Provider itself remains strict by default; set refreshTokenReuseInterval: 0 on mcp() to disable the overlap window.

Inside the window, reuse of a rotated refresh token is not treated as replay, so the token family is not revoked. An attacker who replays a stolen bearer refresh token within 30 seconds of the legitimate refresh gets the replacement refresh token, as long as the retry asks for the same scopes and resources. A DPoP-bound refresh token also needs a valid DPoP proof from the key it is bound to. Most MCP clients are public clients with no secret, so nothing else stops a bearer token retry. Set refreshTokenReuseInterval: 0 unless your clients lose refresh responses; see [Refresh tokens](https://better-auth.com/docs/plugins/oauth-provider/tokens#refresh-tokens).

By default, D1 enforces that foreign key constraints are valid within all queries and migrations.

## Defer foreign key constraints
D1's foreign key enforcement is equivalent to SQLite's `PRAGMA foreign_keys = on` directive.

# Remote MCP server: authentication and Streamable HTTP on MainWorker

Research for issue #301 (map #295, feeds #302). Researched on 2026-11-20 against the pins in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`better-auth` 1.7.25, `@alchemy.run/better-auth` 2.0.0-beta.87, `effect` 4.1.4). Throwaway branch, never merged.

Question: which OAuth stack and MCP transport should serve `/mcp` on `MainWorker`, how does an MCP access token resolve to a Person, an Organization and an `Actor`, and how does a revoked grant, a removed Person or a banned user fail the next request?

Sources were read from the published npm tarballs at the exact versions named (`npm pack <pkg>@<version>`), from the MCP specification at revision 2026-07-28, and from Cloudflare's docs. Line numbers refer to the files inside each tarball.

## Verdict

- **Package name.** At 1.7.25, Better Auth's MCP support is the separate package **`@better-auth/mcp`**. It is built on **`@better-auth/oauth-provider`**, and needs the `jwt()` plugin from `better-auth/plugins`. `better-auth/plugins` has no `mcp` or `oidcProvider` export at 1.7.25, and none at the installed 1.7.11 either. Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD) are a third package, `@better-auth/cimd`.
- **Use Better Auth, not `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider`.** The Cloudflare library keeps grants and tokens only in a KV namespace bound as `OAUTH_KV`. KV is eventually consistent for up to 60 s, and SPEC §6.2 forbids KV for anything that must be revoked at once. It would also create a second identity store beside Better Auth, which ADR 0022 rejected ("two session truths and two revocation paths").
- **Better Auth alone does not satisfy the revocation rule.** With `mcp()`, access tokens are JWTs, and `requireMcpAuth` checks them only against the signing keys, with no database read. Better Auth's refresh grant does not check `banned`, consent or the browser session. SurveyBeat's own `/auth/logout` deletes `auth_session` with raw SQL, which skips Better Auth's token-revocation hook. **So SurveyBeat needs its own check on every request:** one D1 query (the user is not banned, and a consent row for this user, client and Person still exists) and one Durable Object call (the Person is active and is a Lead).
- **Transport.** Serve MCP 2026-07-28 statelessly, one request per server instance. Effect 4.1.4 ships `effect/ai/McpServer.layerHttpRequestScoped` for exactly this case on serverless hosts. Its tools are Effect Schema natively, so SPEC §6.1's "one schema … shared by … the AI tool definitions" holds without an adapter. ## 2. What the MCP spec requires (revision 2026-07-28)

Quoted from <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization> and `…/authorization/client-registration`:

- Servers "MUST implement OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728)". Clients "MUST use" it to find the authorization server.
- "MCP servers MUST validate that access tokens were issued specifically for them as the intended audience, according to RFC 8707 Section 2 … Invalid or expired tokens MUST receive an HTTP 401 response." The status codes are 401 for an invalid token, 403 for "Invalid scopes or insufficient permissions" and 400 for a malformed request.
- "Authorization MUST be included in every HTTP request", as `Authorization: Bearer`, and tokens "MUST NOT be included in the URI query string".
- Servers "SHOULD NOT include `offline_access` in WWW-Authenticate scope or Protected Resource Metadata `scopes_supported`". Clients "MUST NOT assume refresh tokens will be issued".
- The client's registration order is: pre-registered, then CIMD "if the Authorization Server indicates that it supports them (via `client_id_metadata_document_supported`)", then Dynamic Client Registration. The spec says "Dynamic Client Registration is deprecated. New implementations should use Client ID Metadata Documents instead."

`mcp()` handles these server-side duties: it publishes RFC 9728 metadata, binds the audience, and `requireMcpAuth` sends a JSON-RPC 401 with the RFC 9728 `WWW-Authenticate` header or a 403 `insufficient_scope` challenge (`@better-auth/mcp@1.7.25/dist/index.mjs` lines 25–96, 236–262).

## 4. How a token is issued and checked in Better Auth 1.7.25

All of this is from `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25/dist/authorize-BJStuGWz.mjs` unless noted.

1. **Access tokens are JWTs when a resource is set.** `const isJwtAccessToken = REDACTED && !opts.disableJwtPlugin;` (line 2078). `mcp()` always sets the resource, so MCP access tokens are signed JWTs with `sub`, `azp` (the client), `aud`, `sid`, `scope` and `exp`. The default lifetime is 3600 s (`accessTokenExpiresIn: 3600`, defaults at lines 7016–7030). Tokens and secrets are stored hashed (`storeTokens: "hashed"`, line 7026). A JWT access token has no database row: the schema comment says the `oauthAccessToken` model is "an opaque access token sent when there is no resource audience claim" (line 6809).
2. **`requireMcpAuth` checks only the signature.** It calls `verifyAccessTokenRequest` with the local JWKS (`@better-auth/mcp/dist/index.mjs` lines 236–262). That checks the signature, issuer, audience, expiry and the `azp` claim. A database is read only when `remoteVerify` (HTTP introspection) is configured (`@better-auth/core@1.7.25/dist/oauth2/verify.mjs` lines 209–245). A revoked grant therefore keeps working for up to `accessTokenExpiresIn`.
3. **Introspection checks the session but needs a confidential client.** `validateJwtAccessToken` and `validateOpaqueAccessToken` mark a token inactive when its session row is gone or the client is disabled (lines 2543–2588, 2594–2626). `/oauth2/introspect` rejects callers without `client_id` and a secret (lines 2805–2812), and the in-process `validateAccessToken` is marked `@internal`. MCP clients are public clients, so using this path would mean registering a confidential resource-server client just to call our own Worker.
4. **Deleting a session does not end an MCP grant.**
   - `oauthRefreshToken.sessionId` and `oauthAccessToken.sessionId` reference `session.id` with `onDelete: "set null"` (lines 6726–6760, 6820–6850). D1 enforces foreign keys by default (<https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/sql-api/foreign-keys/>), so deleting the session clears the link. A token whose `sessionId` is null skips the session check in step 3.
   - Better Auth's revocation runs in a `session.delete` database hook that returns early `if (!hookCtx)` (line 7240). SurveyBeat's `deleteSession` is a raw `DELETE FROM auth_session WHERE id = ?` (`packages/cloudflare/src/MainWorker.ts`), so the hook never runs.
   - Even when the hook runs, "`offline_access` refresh tokens survive so long-lived API access can outlive the browser session" (comment at line 2888).
5. **The refresh grant checks only the token and that the user exists.** `handleRefreshTokenGrant` (lines 2404–2480) checks the client, the token row, `expiresAt`, `revoked` and the scopes, then `findUserById` (line 2475). It does not check `banned`, the consent row or the session.
6. **`banned` is enforced only when a session is created.** The admin plugin throws `BANNED_USER` in a `session.create.before` hook (`better-auth@1.7.25/dist/plugins/admin/admin.mjs` lines 33–50). `banUser` then calls `deleteUserSessions` (`routes.mjs` line 551). Neither touches OAuth refresh tokens, so a banned user's MCP client can keep refreshing. This confirms ADR 0024's note that Better Auth enforces `banned` only on its own endpoints.
7. **Consent is a stable, per-reference row.** At consent, Better Auth creates or updates an `oauthConsent` row keyed by `clientId`, `userId` and `referenceId` (lines 240–275). Deleting a consent (`/oauth2/delete-consent`) removes only that row. It does not revoke tokens (`deleteConsentEndpoint`, line 5836).
8. **Hooks for an Organization/Person choice.** `postLogin` (`page`, `shouldRedirect`, `consentReferenceId`) runs "After login and before consent, request the user to select an additional choice … For example, allow selection of an organization or team", and `consentReferenceId` "ties to the consent reference_id" (`dist/oauth-kpy9mh0t.d.mts` lines 1667–1700). `customAccessTokenClaims({ user, referenceId, scopes, … })` adds claims to the JWT (line 1838). The `referenceId` is stored on the consent, refresh and access-token rows and passed to the claim builder at issuance.

**Conclusion.** No Better Auth setting at 1.7.25 makes "a revoked grant fails the next request" true for MCP. SurveyBeat has to add its own check on every request, and that check must read a row that revocation deletes.

## 5. Resolving the token to a Person, an Organization and an Actor

How it works today: `checkSession` (`packages/domain/src/people/SignInFlow.ts`) authenticates the cookie and reads the chosen Organization from `auth_session_organization`. It then asks the Organization object for `activePerson(authUserId)`, which runs `person.auth_user_id = ? AND person.removed_at IS NULL` (`packages/cloudflare/src/organization/Directory.ts`). Domain commands build the `Actor` (`personId`, `organizationAdmin`, `roles`) with `actorOf`, which skips removed Persons and inactive Memberships (`packages/domain/src/people/Directory.ts`). `can(actor, action, resource)` decides each action (`packages/domain/src/people/Permissions.ts`).

Proposed MCP path:

1. **Authorize.**
   - `loginPage` is the existing email-code or magic-link screen. SurveyBeat's `/auth/email-code/verify` posts to Better Auth's `/auth/sign-in/email-otp` with a synthetic body (`BetterAuthIdentityProvider.ts`). It must forward the signed `oauth_query`, because the provider's before-hook matches on `ctx.body.oauth_query` to resume the authorization (lines 7268–7290).
   - The `postLogin` page reuses the Organization picker (`candidatesFor`, ADR 0023). It offers only candidates whose Person is a Lead of at least one Team.
   - `consentReferenceId` returns `"<OrganizationId>:<PersonId>"`. A Person who is removed and added again gets a new `PersonId`, so the old grant can never match the new Person.
2. **Issue.** `customAccessTokenClaims` copies the `referenceId` into a private claim (for example `https://surveybeat.app/person`). The consent page shows the Organization name and the scopes.
3. **Check on every `/mcp` request.**
   1. Verify the JWT with `requireMcpAuth`, or with `createMcpProtectedRequestHandler` if the issuer and audience must be explicit. Failure: 401 with the RFC 9728 challenge.
   2. **One D1 query.** The `auth_user` row exists. `banned` is false, or `banExpires` has passed. A consent row exists for (`userId = sub`, `clientId = azp`, `referenceId = claim`). Optionally, the client is not `disabled`. Any failure means the grant was revoked, deleted or banned: answer 401 `invalid_token`, so the client discards the token. This is the MCP equivalent of ADR 0023's "deleting the row is the revocation".
   3. **One Organization DO call.** `activePerson(sub)` returns the Person, its id equals the claim's `PersonId`, and `actorOf` shows `lead` on at least one Team. A removed Person answers 401. A Person with no Lead role (including an Organization admin who leads no Team, ADR 0003) answers 403. The answer status here is a proposal: the spec defines 401 and 403 but not this particular split.
   4. Give the tool handlers the `Actor`. Each tool calls the same `Organization*` services as the HttpApi handlers, so `can(...)`, ADR 0004's minimum group size and the #302 privacy registry apply unchanged.
4. **Revoke.**
   - *Disconnect an assistant* (a new settings action): delete the consent row, and mark the refresh tokens for (`userId`, `clientId`) revoked as cleanup. The next request fails at step 3.2.
   - *Person removed*: step 3.3 fails at once. No D1 write is needed.
   - *Ban*: step 3.2 fails at once.
   - *Browser sign-out*: leaves the MCP grant in place, by design. The grant is the consent, not the cookie, matching OAuth's `offline_access` semantics. Record this choice in the ADR. The alternative is to also require the JWT's `sid` session row, but that breaks every assistant at the 30-day session expiry.

Cost: one JWKS read (in-process), one D1 query and one DO RPC per MCP request. That is one more D1 read than a cookie request, which today is `getSession` plus `auth_session_organization` plus the DO.

# Remote MCP server: authentication and Streamable HTTP on MainWorker

Research for issue #301 (map #295, feeds #302). Researched on 2026-11-20 against the pins in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`better-auth` 1.7.25, `@alchemy.run/better-auth` 2.0.0-beta.87, `effect` 4.1.4). Throwaway branch, never merged.

Question: which OAuth stack and MCP transport should serve `/mcp` on `MainWorker`, how does an MCP access token resolve to a Person, an Organization and an `Actor`, and how does a revoked grant, a removed Person or a banned user fail the next request?

Sources were read from the published npm tarballs at the exact versions named (`npm pack <pkg>@<version>`), from the MCP specification at revision 2026-07-28, and from Cloudflare's docs. Line numbers refer to the files inside each tarball.

## Verdict

- **Package name.** At 1.7.25, Better Auth's MCP support is the separate package **`@better-auth/mcp`**. It is built on **`@better-auth/oauth-provider`**, and needs the `jwt()` plugin from `better-auth/plugins`. `better-auth/plugins` has no `mcp` or `oidcProvider` export at 1.7.25, and none at the installed 1.7.11 either. Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD) are a third package, `@better-auth/cimd`.
- **Use Better Auth, not `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider`.** The Cloudflare library keeps grants and tokens only in a KV namespace bound as `OAUTH_KV`. KV is eventually consistent for up to 60 s, and SPEC §6.2 forbids KV for anything that must be revoked at once. It would also create a second identity store beside Better Auth, which ADR 0022 rejected ("two session truths and two revocation paths").
- **Better Auth alone does not satisfy the revocation rule.** With `mcp()`, access tokens are JWTs, and `requireMcpAuth` checks them only against the signing keys, with no database read. Better Auth's refresh grant does not check `banned`, consent or the browser session. SurveyBeat's own `/auth/logout` deletes `auth_session` with raw SQL, which skips Better Auth's token-revocation hook. **So SurveyBeat needs its own check on every request:** one D1 query (the user is not banned, and a consent row for this user, client and Person still exists) and one Durable Object call (the Person is active and is a Lead).

## 2. What the MCP spec requires (revision 2026-07-28)

Quoted from <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization> and `…/authorization/client-registration`:

- Servers "MUST implement OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728)". Clients "MUST use" it to find the authorization server.
- "MCP servers MUST validate that access tokens were issued specifically for them as the intended audience, according to RFC 8707 Section 2 … Invalid or expired tokens MUST receive an HTTP 401 response." The status codes are 401 for an invalid token, 403 for "Invalid scopes or insufficient permissions" and 400 for a malformed request.
- "Authorization MUST be included in every HTTP request", as `Authorization: Bearer`, and tokens "MUST NOT be included in the URI query string".
- Servers "SHOULD NOT include `offline_access` in WWW-Authenticate scope or Protected Resource Metadata `scopes_supported`". Clients "MUST NOT assume refresh tokens will be issued".
- The client's registration order is: pre-registered, then CIMD "if the Authorization Server indicates that it supports them (via `client_id_metadata_document_supported`)", then Dynamic Client Registration. The spec says "Dynamic Client Registration is deprecated. New implementations should use Client ID Metadata Documents instead."

`mcp()` handles these server-side duties: it publishes RFC 9728 metadata, binds the audience, and `requireMcpAuth` sends a JSON-RPC 401 with the RFC 9728 `WWW-Authenticate` header or a 403 `insufficient_scope` challenge (`@better-auth/mcp@1.7.25/dist/index.mjs` lines 25–96, 236–262).

## 4. How a token is issued and checked in Better Auth 1.7.25

All of this is from `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25/dist/authorize-BJStuGWz.mjs` unless noted.

1. **Access tokens are JWTs when a resource is set.** `const isJwtAccessToken = REDACTED && !opts.disableJwtPlugin;` (line 2078). `mcp()` always sets the resource, so MCP access tokens are signed JWTs with `sub`, `azp` (the client), `aud`, `sid`, `scope` and `exp`. The default lifetime is 3600 s (`accessTokenExpiresIn: 3600`, defaults at lines 7016–7030). Tokens and secrets are stored hashed (`storeTokens: "hashed"`, line 7026). A JWT access token has no database row: the schema comment says the `oauthAccessToken` model is "an opaque access token sent when there is no resource audience claim" (line 6809).
2. **`requireMcpAuth` checks only the signature.** It calls `verifyAccessTokenRequest` with the local JWKS (`@better-auth/mcp/dist/index.mjs` lines 236–262). That checks the signature, issuer, audience, expiry and the `azp` claim. A database is read only when `remoteVerify` (HTTP introspection) is configured (`@better-auth/core@1.7.25/dist/oauth2/verify.mjs` lines 209–245). A revoked grant therefore keeps working for up to `accessTokenExpiresIn`.
3. **Introspection checks the session but needs a confidential client.** `validateJwtAccessToken` and `validateOpaqueAccessToken` mark a token inactive when its session row is gone or the client is disabled (lines 2543–2588, 2594–2626). `/oauth2/introspect` rejects callers without `client_id` and a secret (lines 2805–2812), and the in-process `validateAccessToken` is marked `@internal`. MCP clients are public clients, so using this path would mean registering a confidential resource-server client just to call our own Worker.
4. **Deleting a session does not end an MCP grant.**
   - `oauthRefreshToken.sessionId` and `oauthAccessToken.sessionId` reference `session.id` with `onDelete: "set null"` (lines 6726–6760, 6820–6850). D1 enforces foreign keys by default (<https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/sql-api/foreign-keys/>), so deleting the session clears the link. A token whose `sessionId` is null skips the session check in step 3.
   - Better Auth's revocation runs in a `session.delete` database hook that returns early `if (!hookCtx)` (line 7240). SurveyBeat's `deleteSession` is a raw `DELETE FROM auth_session WHERE id = ?` (`packages/cloudflare/src/MainWorker.ts`), so the hook never runs.
   - Even when the hook runs, "`offline_access` refresh tokens survive so long-lived API access can outlive the browser session" (comment at line 2888).
5. **The refresh grant checks only the token and that the user exists.** `handleRefreshTokenGrant` (lines 2404–2480) checks the client, the token row, `expiresAt`, `revoked` and the scopes, then `findUserById` (line 2475). It does not check `banned`, the consent row or the session.
6. **`banned` is enforced only when a session is created.** The admin plugin throws `BANNED_USER` in a `session.create.before` hook (`better-auth@1.7.25/dist/plugins/admin/admin.mjs` lines 33–50). `banUser` then calls `deleteUserSessions` (`routes.mjs` line 551). Neither touches OAuth refresh tokens, so a banned user's MCP client can keep refreshing. This confirms ADR 0024's note that Better Auth enforces `banned` only on its own endpoints.
7. **Consent is a stable, per-reference row.** At consent, Better Auth creates or updates an `oauthConsent` row keyed by `clientId`, `userId` and `referenceId` (lines 240–275). Deleting a consent (`/oauth2/delete-consent`) removes only that row. It does not revoke tokens (`deleteConsentEndpoint`, line 5836).
8. **Hooks for an Organization/Person choice.** `postLogin` (`page`, `shouldRedirect`, `consentReferenceId`) runs "After login and before consent, request the user to select an additional choice … For example, allow selection of an organization or team", and `consentReferenceId` "ties to the consent reference_id" (`dist/oauth-kpy9mh0t.d.mts` lines 1667–1700). `customAccessTokenClaims({ user, referenceId, scopes, … })` adds claims to the JWT (line 1838). The `referenceId` is stored on the consent, refresh and access-token rows and passed to the claim builder at issuance.

**Conclusion.** No Better Auth setting at 1.7.25 makes "a revoked grant fails the next request" true for MCP. SurveyBeat has to add its own check on every request, and that check must read a row that revocation deletes.

## 5. Resolving the token to a Person, an Organization and an Actor

How it works today: `checkSession` (`packages/domain/src/people/SignInFlow.ts`) authenticates the cookie and reads the chosen Organization from `auth_session_organization`. It then asks the Organization object for `activePerson(authUserId)`, which runs `person.auth_user_id = ? AND person.removed_at IS NULL` (`packages/cloudflare/src/organization/Directory.ts`). Domain commands build the `Actor` (`personId`, `organizationAdmin`, `roles`) with `actorOf`, which skips removed Persons and inactive Memberships (`packages/domain/src/people/Directory.ts`). `can(actor, action, resource)` decides each action (`packages/domain/src/people/Permissions.ts`).

Proposed MCP path:

1. **Authorize.**
   - `loginPage` is the existing email-code or magic-link screen. SurveyBeat's `/auth/email-code/verify` posts to Better Auth's `/auth/sign-in/email-otp` with a synthetic body (`BetterAuthIdentityProvider.ts`). It must forward the signed `oauth_query`, because the provider's before-hook matches on `ctx.body.oauth_query` to resume the authorization (lines 7268–7290).
   - The `postLogin` page reuses the Organization picker (`candidatesFor`, ADR 0023). It offers only candidates whose Person is a Lead of at least one Team.
   - `consentReferenceId` returns `"<OrganizationId>:<PersonId>"`. A Person who is removed and added again gets a new `PersonId`, so the old grant can never match the new Person.
2. **Issue.** `customAccessTokenClaims` copies the `referenceId` into a private claim (for example `https://surveybeat.app/person`). The consent page shows the Organization name and the scopes.
3. **Check on every `/mcp` request.**
   1. Verify the JWT with `requireMcpAuth`, or with `createMcpProtectedRequestHandler` if the issuer and audience must be explicit. Failure: 401 with the RFC 9728 challenge.
   2. **One D1 query.** The `auth_user` row exists. `banned` is false, or `banExpires` has passed. A consent row exists for (`userId = sub`, `clientId = azp`, `referenceId = claim`). Optionally, the client is not `disabled`. Any failure means the grant was revoked, deleted or banned: answer 401 `invalid_token`, so the client discards the token. This is the MCP equivalent of ADR 0023's "deleting the row is the revocation".
   3. **One Organization DO call.** `activePerson(sub)` returns the Person, its id equals the claim's `PersonId`, and `actorOf` shows `lead` on at least one Team. A removed Person answers 401. A Person with no Lead role (including an Organization admin who leads no Team, ADR 0003) answers 403. The answer status here is a proposal: the spec defines 401 and 403 but not this particular split.
   4. Give the tool handlers the `Actor`. Each tool calls the same `Organization*` services as the HttpApi handlers, so `can(...)`, ADR 0004's minimum group size and the #302 privacy registry apply unchanged.
4. **Revoke.**
   - *Disconnect an assistant* (a new settings action): delete the consent row, and mark the refresh tokens for (`userId`, `clientId`) revoked as cleanup. The next request fails at step 3.2.
   - *Person removed*: step 3.3 fails at once. No D1 write is needed.
   - *Ban*: step 3.2 fails at once.
   - *Browser sign-out*: leaves the MCP grant in place, by design. The grant is the consent, not the cookie, matching OAuth's `offline_access` semantics. Record this choice in the ADR. The alternative is to also require the JWT's `sid` session row, but that breaks every assistant at the 30-day session expiry.

Cost: one JWKS read (in-process), one D1 query and one DO RPC per MCP request. That is one more D1 read than a cookie request, which today is `getSession` plus `auth_session_organization` plus the DO.

## 6. CIMD and client registration on Workers

- Enable `cimd({ metadataProfile: "mcp-2026-07-28", fetchClientMetadataResource })`. Its bundled `@better-auth/cimd/node` transport imports `node:dns/promises`, `node:https`, `node:net` and `node:stream`, and pins the connection to a resolved IP (`dist/node.mjs` lines 1–40). - Turn on `global_fetch_strictly_public` so outbound `fetch` "will strictly route requests as if they were made on the public Internet" (<https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/compatibility-flags/#global-fetch-strictly-public>). Cloudflare's own provider requires the same flag for CIMD.
- Keep Dynamic Client Registration off unless a target assistant cannot use CIMD (§9). DCR is deprecated in 2026-07-28 and is off by default in Better Auth (`allowDynamicClientRegistration: false`, line 7021).

## 7. Routing on MainWorker

- Today `MainWorker` forwards to Better Auth only the `/auth/*` paths it does not answer itself. Better Auth's issuer is its base URL plus `basePath: "/auth"`, and its docs say "a server with a base path serves them at the issuer-inserted location rather than the bare root". So `MainWorker` must also forward these paths to `authInstance.fetch`:
  - `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/auth`
  - `/.well-known/openid-configuration/auth`
  - `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`

  The `mcp()` plugin answers the last two in its `onRequest` (`dist/index.mjs` lines 186–203).
- `resource` must be the canonical HTTPS URL `https://<app host>/mcp` for each stage. `mcp()` rejects a query, a fragment, credentials and non-loopback HTTP (`validateMcpResource`). The local stage on `http://localhost:1337` passes as loopback.
- `/mcp` is not an HttpApi endpoint, so `PrivacyRegistry.ts` will not catch it. #302's MCP privacy registry has to cover it (already planned there).

1. **Authorization server:** `@better-auth/mcp` `mcp({ resource: "https://<host>/mcp", loginPage, consentPage, postLogin: { page, shouldRedirect, consentReferenceId }, customAccessTokenClaims, scopes, refreshTokenReuseInterval: 0, schema: { …auth_ model names } })`, plus `jwt({ schema: { jwks: { modelName: "auth_jwks" } } })` and `@better-auth/cimd` with a `fetch` transport. One new numbered migration, for example `packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations/0011_mcp_oauth.sql`, with its SHA-256 added to `d1-migrations.lock.json`. It creates these tables with the `auth_` prefix, set through each plugin's `schema.<model>.modelName`:

- `auth_oauth_client`, `auth_oauth_resource`, `auth_oauth_client_resource` (unique `clientId` + `resourceId`, cascade).

- `auth_oauth_access_token`: the same shape. It is used only for opaque tokens, but the schema needs it.
- `auth_oauth_consent`: `clientId`, `userId`, `referenceId`, `scopes`, `resources`. This is the grant row the per-request check reads.
- `auth_oauth_client_assertion`.

The models are from `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25` `dist/authorize-BJStuGWz.mjs` lines 6420–6960. Index `auth_oauth_consent (userId, clientId, referenceId)` for the per-request lookup. None of these tables holds survey content, which matches SPEC §6.2's limits on D1.

None. `person.auth_user_id`, `person.removed_at` and the Memberships with role `lead` already answer "is this an active Lead". `activePerson` plus `actorOf` in the Organization object are enough. One optional addition is an Organization-object read that returns the `Actor` in one RPC, so the MCP middleware does not need a second call.
